subject: Post-call: Sponsor roadmap, acceptance criteria & contracting next steps
message_1_subject: Post-call: Sponsor roadmap, acceptance criteria & contracting next steps
message_1_body:
Ethan —

Thanks again for a productive conversation earlier. Below is a concise recap for your leadership and procurement teams so we have aligned acceptance criteria, risks, and the contracting path. Let me know if I missed anything.

Key pain points (what we heard)
- Latency spikes during morning batch jobs (95th pctl ~ 1.2s, target <= 400ms)
- Data residency / EU-bound PII for 10% of requests (audit requirement)
- Unpredictable token costs when usage scales beyond pilot

Business goals (90-day pilot)
- Validate end-to-end 95th pctl < 500ms for interactive flows
- Keep incremental inference spend growth <= 30% vs. current baseline
- Verify QPS scaling to sustained 200 r/s with autoscaling fallback

Acceptance criteria for pilot (what success looks like)
1) Performance: 95th pctl latency < 500ms under representative load for 3 consecutive days
2) Security: Redwood Private or VPC deployment passes your security checklist OR we provide SOC2 + evidence for hosted with contractual guarantees
3) Cost transparency: per-route token accounting and forecast for month-on-month scaling

Top risks and potential escalations
- If NovaCorp requires on-prem deployment during pilot, lead time for env prep ~ 4–6 weeks and will impact timeline
- SOC2 evidence: we can share our report, but an accelerated audit or additional POA&M may be requested by your security team
- Procurement timing: if PO issuance lags > 30 days, pilot start date will slip; escalation path suggested is your VP of Engineering -> our Head of Sales (Ben)

Contracting / procurement path (recommended)
- Step A: We will send a short SOW (scope + pilot KPIs) for signature (DocuSign link below).
- Step B: Procurement issues PO referencing the signed SOW and our standard MSA (we can accept NovaCorp redlines on data residency appendix).
- Step C: Kickoff & environment provisioning (2 business days for hosted; 4–6 weeks for private on-prem).

Immediate next steps (owners & timing)
- Monica: share draft SOW + pilot scope by Tue 21 Jul (attached: pilot-scope.xlsx, SLA-template.pdf)
- Ben: produce edge pricing estimate for 200 r/s steady state and reserved discount options by Wed 22 Jul
- Ethan / Procurement: confirm if your security team will accept hosted SOC2 evidence or if on-prem is required by Fri 24 Jul

Attachments: pilot-scope.xlsx (pilot milestones + test plan), SLA-template.pdf (standard SLO language).

Drive links / DocuSign: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cNOVACORP-pilot — DocuSign SOW (we will populate once scope approved).

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to SOW.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

message_2_subject: Re: Post-call: Sponsor roadmap, acceptance criteria & contracting next steps
message_2_body:
Ethan / team —

Following Monica's excellent summary, I attached a high-level pricing estimate and three contracting options so procurement has a starting point: pricing-estimate.xlsx. Quick notes: 
- Option A (Pilot Hosted): month-to-month, no commit, higher unit; suitable if you want <2 week turn-up.
- Option B (Pilot + Reserved Burst): 3-month pilot with reserved capacity burst and modest discount (recommended if you expect to reach sustained QPS quickly).
- Option C (Private / On-prem): one-time infra onboarding + support retainer; longer lead-time.

Procurement contacts we typically work with (if helpful):
- Sara Lim, Head of Vendor Ops — sara.lim@redwood.inference
- Finance AP: ap@redwood.inference (we accept standard PO workflows)

I'll open a DocuSign envelope with the draft SOW (linked) and include the pricing sheet. If you confirm that hosted SOC2 is acceptable, we can proceed without a private deployment and save ~4 weeks.

Ben
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.inference

Attachments: pricing-estimate.xlsx
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abc123-SOW
